newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT says rate scheme likely to get nod.
newsitem.headline: PLDT says rate scheme likely to get nod.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) has expressed optimism that its proposed new rate structure which calls for a metering scheme would be approved by regulatory authorities.

"We believe it will gain acceptance as it addresses the needs and interests of all the parties concerned," PLDT chairman Roberto Romulo and president Antonio Cojuangco said in the company's 1996 annual report released on Wednesday ahead of the annual stockholders meeting.

The officials said the "rate rebalancing" petition submitted to the National Telecommunications Commission would enable the company to build fixed lines without relying on the dwindling margins from international gateway opeations.

PLDT proposes to lower its international toll rates and plans to begin metering local calls to make up for the reduction in international call rates. It has also sought an increase in basic local phone charges.
At present, PLDT charges a monthly flat rates for local phone service regardless of the number and length of calls.
